note: Identity only: every tool is named by version string and SHA-256, with the
provenance needed to obtain or rebuild it.  No local path appears here.
Where the tools live on this machine is a local setting: the environment
variable XENO_TOOLCHAIN_DIR, or config/toolchain-local.json (untracked).

ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7.role: cc1 of every GCC 2.96-family compile contract (game and runtime C)
ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7.version: gcc 2.96-ee-001003-1 (cc1), locally patched: realconv + lp7 + fsv3

rebuild: Download the base archive and check its SHA-256.
Extract lib/gcc-lib/ee/2.96-ee-001003-1/{cc1,cpp0} and bin/ee-gcc into <root>/ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv3-v1/bin/.
cpp0 and ee-gcc are used unmodified.
Apply the patches below to cc1, in file-offset order (eight single-byte patches and four multi-byte patches: fsv1 and fsv3); the result must hash to the cc1 SHA-256 above.

note: Each entry patches the bytes of the extracted cc1 at `file_offset` (one byte, except the fsv1 and fsv3 entries, which replace the given hex strings).
`old` must be the byte already there; `new` replaces it.
The six `realconv` patches turn the six MASK_MIPS5900 conversion gates
of the bundled e-type float code into unconditional jumps, so decimal
literals round the way the original compiler rounded them.
The two `lp7` patches raise the R5900 short-loop padding gate and loop
bound in mips_r5900_lengthen_loops from 4 to 6, which reproduces the
7-d padding ten original game objects carry.
The `fsv1` patch (user decision 2026-09-23, reports/cc1-fsv-clause1-losum.md)
rewrites clause 1 of the alias-analysis helper fixed_scalar_and_varying_struct_p
(cc1 0x080ee624) so that a LO_SUM address of the scalar mem1 counts as
non-varying: a store to a split (lui/%lo) global scalar no longer blocks a
later struct-field load with a varying address in sched1, as the original
CardMainProc (OV10 0x00A03AA0) shows. Clause 2 and rtx_varies_p are unchanged.
The three `fsv3` patches (user decision 2026-09-23, reports/cc1-fsv3-alias.md)
supersede fsv1 on top of it: clause 2 treats a LO_SUM mem2 address as non-varying
too (symmetric LO_SUM rule), and make_decl_rtl jumps to an 88-byte cave written
over debug_rtx_list (only called by the debug-only debug_rtx_find) that gives the
MEM of a non-function, non-small-data decl its type alias set by calling
set_mem_attributes before DECL_RTL is stored. The cave source is cave.s in the release.
Why this is a patched binary and not a published one (public-compiler hunt,
2026-09-12, .work/attempts/tu-public-compiler-hunt/attempt-1/artifact.json):
all 15 public ee-gcc* entries of the pinned decompme catalog revision were
tested, and none produces both the rounded decimal literals and the 7-d
short-loop padding the original bytes carry. The flag hypothesis is dead
mechanically: the complete TARGET_SWITCHES/TARGET_OPTIONS tables were read
out of every candidate ELF and no entry names rounding, truncation, loops or
the R5900 short-loop erratum, and the padding pass is gated on the same
MASK_MIPS5900 bit with its thresholds as immediate bytes in code.
lp7's value is SCE's own: ps2-ee-toolchain ee/gcc/config/mips/mips.c:8717
(SCE 2.9-ee-991111, GPL-2.0-or-later) reads `for (; distance <= 6;
distance++) emit_insn_before (gen_nop (), insn);`, and the public
ee-gcc2.9-991111 cc1 carries `cmp $0x6` at 0x081ad7cc and 0x081ad7e4 - the
same two instruction slots these patches set to 6 in the 2.96 binary, whose
catalog build moved the pass after delay-slot filling, split it into a
JUMP_INSN and a SEQUENCE arm and lowered both to 4. So the patch restores a
constant SCE shipped rather than inventing one; the build that carries it on
the JUMP arm only is not public.
The asymmetry is evidenced from both sides: the ten 7-d objects require 6 on
the JUMP arm, and raising the SEQUENCE arm to 6 as well breaks 17 of the 101
accepted C TUs, so 4 there is required by the accepted corpus.
Caveat that keeps original_distribution_proven false: the unpatched public
cc1 currently compiles all 101 accepted TUs to identical assembly and passes
the whole-file gate, because the recovered corpus is still blind to both
patches (0 of its 71 decimal literals discriminate rounding, 0 TUs reach the
JUMP arm). The original bytes are not blind: 343 rounded-evidence constants
and the ten padded objects. A clean witness is xglRenderSyncMove (main
0x0022CC40, five nops, body 7, unfilled delay slot).

patches.governs: e-type -> SFmode (double literal narrowed to float)
decimal -> e-type, final round to target precision
after gen_rtx_MEM: jmp to the cave at 0x080d927c (replaces the DECL_RTL store and add $0x18,%esp)
non-FUNCTION_DECL decl with int_size_in_bytes (TREE_TYPE) <= 0 or > mips_section_threshold: set_mem_attributes (mem, decl, 1) with DECL_RTL NULL, then DECL_RTL = mem; resume at 0x080d1e73

clause 1 (MEM_SCALAR_P (mem1) && MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (mem2) && !varies_p (mem1_addr) && varies_p (mem2_addr) -> no dependence): skip varies_p (mem1_addr), treating it as 0, when GET_CODE (mem1_addr) == LO_SUM (cmpb $0x90,(%eax))
clause 2: a LO_SUM mem2_addr counts as non-varying (cmpb $0x90,(%eax))
cmp $imm8,%esi: JUMP_INSN arm gate, pad only when the loop distance d <= imm
cmp $imm8,%ebx: JUMP_INSN arm nop-emission loop bound, i = d .. imm

ee-as-la29-vsqrt.role: assembler of every game and runtime object (the -G of the object is passed per object)
ee-as-la29-vsqrt.version: GNU assembler 2.9-ee-991111, locally patched: memmove + vsqrt + nolabel

rebuild: Check out the commit above (the `ee` binutils 2.9 tree it carries).
Apply `source_diff` below.
configure --target=ee --disable-nls --disable-shared, then build gas; install build/gas/as-new as ee-as (no strip).

The build is not bit-reproducible across host compilers; the SHA-256 above is this project's build (host gcc 16.1.1).  A differently built ee-as that assembles the same bytes also reproduces the images, so the hash check can be relaxed with XENO_TOOLCHAIN_ALLOW=ee-as-la29-vsqrt (the build then says so).
patch_reasons: md_convert_frag copies an expanded alternative over its own destination; memcpy corrupts the overlap on a modern libc, memmove does not.  Behaviour only, not an encoding change.
The vsqrt base opcode carries bits 21-22 = 01 in every original word, as GNU as 2.10-ee-001003-1 and ps2dev binutils encode it; the 2.9 table has 00 and assembles the wrong word silently.

append_insn moved every label pending before an instruction to after the hazard nops it inserts; the original objects keep such labels before the nop (14 mtc1 sites, e.g. CardMainProc 0x00A085E8), so the loop is removed (mips_emit_delays unchanged; user decision 2026-09-24, reports/as-la29-vsqrt-nolabel.md). The build embeds its absolute source paths; the pinned hash is this project's build from .work/tu-migration/as-nolabel-adopt/build/src/tc-mips.c.

ee-as-2.9-plain.role: assembler of the SCE SDK contract's scaffold objects (ee-tu-c991111-G0)

rebuild: The same checkout as ee-as-la29-vsqrt with no patch applied; configure --target=ee --disable-nls --disable-shared, build gas, install build/gas/as-new as ee-as.
Not bit-reproducible across host compilers; see XENO_TOOLCHAIN_ALLOW above.

ps2dev-binutils.role: modern GAS for scaffold data objects and retail blobs, and the linker and objcopy of every unit link

rebuild: configure --target=mips64r5900el-ps2-elf --disable-separate-code --disable-sim --disable-gdb --disable-gdbserver --disable-nls --disable-werror --without-debuginfod --with-python=no
make all-gas all-ld all-binutils && make install-gas install-ld install-binutils
Not bit-reproducible across host compilers; a stock 2.45.1 ps2dev build works.  Relax the hash check with XENO_TOOLCHAIN_ALLOW=ps2dev-binutils.

dvp-as-3eb45ea.role: assembler of every VU microprogram (the DVP assembler; config/vu-build.json contract vu-dvp-as-v1)

rebuild: Check out the commit above; no modification.

Out of tree: configure --target=dvp --disable-nls --disable-werror --disable-gdb --disable-gdbserver --disable-gprofng --disable-sim --disable-gprof --disable-gold --without-debuginfod --without-zstd --without-zlib --disable-shared
make MAKEINFO=true all-gas, then install build/gas/as-new as dvp-as (no strip).
configure excludes ld for this target: there is no dvp linker, and none is needed - the DVP object is linked by the EE linker (config/toolchain-identity.json ps2dev-binutils).

Not bit-reproducible across host compilers; this is this project's build (.work/attempts/ps2-vu-microcode-backend-23). A differently built dvp-as that assembles the same bytes also reproduces the packet, so the hash check can be relaxed with XENO_TOOLCHAIN_ALLOW=dvp-as-3eb45ea (the build then says so).

note: One entry per compile contract of config/objects/<unit>.json.  `compiler`
and `assembler` name a tool above; `flags` is the object's own -O/-G, which
the per-object contract repeats per object.

ee-tu-c991111-G0.gap: No swap-capable 2.9-ee-991111 GAS is pinned; the plain build reproduces every SDK object of this contract.

vu-dvp-as-v1.description: VU microprogram object assembled by the DVP assembler (docs/vu-microcode-unit.md)
vu-dvp-as-v1.note: config/vu-build.json is the contract's authority; this entry names its tools by identity. --fatal-warnings makes the DVP assembler's count warnings errors; -no-abicalls -64 clear the PIC/n32 marks that would make ld speak when the object meets this project's EABI64 objects.

splat.note: The disassembler that regenerates the scaffold.  Pinned in requirements.txt; install it into a virtualenv and point XENO_SPLAT_PYTHON at that interpreter, or let configure.py use the interpreter that runs it.
